answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain custody of 1,000 unique data shards to verify active storage. A verifier requests unpredictable file segments, which agents must return within a set timeframe. An honest agent incurs a baseline disk cost, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost by maintaining independent files. This process acts like a mesa where only distinct shards survive, checked by a sable protocol that audits every access. Should any agent fail to prove retrieval, the saffron ledge of audit threads results in an immediate slash, ensuring no refunds for fakes.
